executive_summary.headline: Critical Security Posture Identified Across 8 Transport Sessions
executive_summary.posture_summary: The investigation identified a CRITICAL security posture. High-risk cryptographic weaknesses or cleartext credential transmission were observed during transport-layer evaluation.
executive_summary.key_findings_summary: The primary drivers of this assessment were: authentication occurred before TLS protection was established; STARTTLS was advertised by the server but was not negotiated by the client; deprecated TLS protocols (TLS 1.0/1.1) were negotiated; legacy or non-AEAD cipher suites were utilized.
executive_summary.transport_security_summary: SecureMailScope analyzed 8 observed POP3/IMAP/SMTP transport session(s) from capture 'lab-mixed-fleet.pcap'. 0 session(s) passed all assessed baseline checks, 6 required review, and 2 had critical transport risks.
executive_summary.ai_anomaly_summary: AI-assisted anomaly prioritization evaluated 8 observed client profiles across 14 transport dimensions. 2 client(s) were prioritized for analyst attention based on relative statistical divergence.
executive_summary.full_text:
SecureMailScope analyzed 8 observed POP3/IMAP/SMTP transport session(s) from capture 'lab-mixed-fleet.pcap'. 0 session(s) passed all assessed baseline checks, 6 required review, and 2 had critical transport risks.

The investigation identified a CRITICAL security posture. High-risk cryptographic weaknesses or cleartext credential transmission were observed during transport-layer evaluation. The primary drivers of this assessment were: authentication occurred before TLS protection was established; STARTTLS was advertised by the server but was not negotiated by the client; deprecated TLS protocols (TLS 1.0/1.1) were negotiated; legacy or non-AEAD cipher suites were utilized.

AI-assisted anomaly prioritization evaluated 8 observed client profiles across 14 transport dimensions. 2 client(s) were prioritized for analyst attention based on relative statistical divergence.

deterministic_findings.title: Cleartext Email Transport
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: This email session continued without TLS protection, allowing application-layer traffic to traverse the observed network path without transport encryption.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: Cleartext email transport exposes message metadata, routing headers, and session contents to passive eavesdropping and traffic manipulation along the transit path.
deterministic_findings.evidence: Identified SMTP session on port 587.; No TLS encryption handshake was negotiated for this session.; Session operated in CLEARTEXT (STARTTLS Offered but Not Used) mode.

evidence_items.description: Identified SMTP session on port 587.
No TLS encryption handshake was negotiated for this session.
Session operated in CLEARTEXT (STARTTLS Offered but Not Used) mode.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Enforce TLS encryption for all email communications using Direct TLS (e.g. port 465/993/995) or mandatory STARTTLS with strict rejection of unencrypted fallbacks.

steps: Configure the affected client to require STARTTLS or the correct implicit-TLS port.
For authenticated submission, reject plaintext fallback after testing clients. Treat public relay policy separately.
Capture again and check the server selection and authentication order.

snippet.scope: Example parameter values for authenticated submission only. Translate to per-service master.cf overrides where appropriate. Requires a working TLS certificate/key. Do not apply globally to a public port-25 relay.

deterministic_findings.title: STARTTLS Available But Not Used
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: The server advertised STARTTLS, but the client continued the SMTP session without upgrading to TLS.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: Transport encryption was available from the server, but the client did not initiate an upgrade. Without mandatory TLS enforcement, the session continued unprotected over cleartext.
deterministic_findings.evidence: Server advertised STARTTLS capability.; No STARTTLS command or TLS handshake was observed.

evidence_items.description: Server advertised STARTTLS capability.
No STARTTLS command or TLS handshake was observed.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Configure the client and server policy to require TLS for this mail flow and reject insecure fallback where operationally appropriate.

steps: Require TLS before advertising or accepting authentication on the submission service.
Update affected clients and rotate potentially exposed credentials through your approved process.
Confirm in a fresh capture that authentication cannot occur in plaintext.

deterministic_findings.title: Authentication Before TLS
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: Transmitting authentication credentials over an unencrypted cleartext session exposes account login data to passive network capture and credential theft.
deterministic_findings.evidence: SMTP authentication command (e.g. AUTH/LOGIN/USER) was observed on the wire.; Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.

evidence_items.description: SMTP authentication command (e.g. AUTH/LOGIN/USER) was observed on the wire.
Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Configure the mail server to mandate STARTTLS before advertising or accepting AUTH commands.

Check both mandatory and opportunistic TLS settings for the intended service.

deterministic_findings.title: Deprecated TLS Version (TLS 1.0)
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: Observed email session negotiated deprecated TLS 1.0 protocol, which is susceptible to known downgrade attacks and lacks modern authenticated encryption.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: TLS 1.0 is formally deprecated under RFC 8996 due to lack of modern cipher constructions, vulnerability to downgrade attacks, and security weaknesses.
deterministic_findings.evidence: Server selected deprecated protocol version TLS 1.0.

evidence_items.description: Server selected deprecated protocol version TLS 1.0.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 on 198.51.100.25 and configure the mail server to require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 as the minimum acceptable protocol version.

steps: Upgrade the affected mail server and client TLS libraries.
Remove the identified weak suites from that service using its version-specific cipher configuration; prefer supported AEAD suites.
Test client compatibility and verify the newly selected cipher in a fresh capture.

deterministic_findings.title: Weak / Deprecated Cipher Suite (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA)
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: The session negotiated weak or deprecated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA, which is vulnerable to cryptanalytic attacks.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: The selected cipher suite (TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA) utilizes obsolete algorithms (such as 64-bit block ciphers like 3DES vulnerable to Sweet32, or stream ciphers like RC4) susceptible to practical collision or plaintext recovery attacks.
deterministic_findings.evidence: Negotiated cipher suite identifier: TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

evidence_items.description: Negotiated cipher suite identifier: TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Disable obsolete cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, DES, EXPORT, NULL) on the mail server and require modern AEAD suites (e.g., AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305).

steps: Prefer ephemeral ECDHE/DHE key exchange where supported; remove static RSA exchange after compatibility testing.
For TLS 1.3 inspect the selected key-share group; the cipher name alone does not prove forward secrecy.

deterministic_findings.title: Static Key Exchange Without Forward Secrecy
deterministic_findings.plain_explanation: The session negotiated a static RSA key exchange cipher suite lacking Perfect Forward Secrecy. Compromise of the server private key allows retroactive decryption of past sessions.
deterministic_findings.why_it_matters: Static key exchange allows an adversary who captures encrypted traffic to decrypt it retroactively if they acquire the server's private key in the future.
deterministic_findings.evidence: Negotiated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA uses static RSA key exchange without ephemeral parameters.

evidence_items.description: Negotiated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA uses static RSA key exchange without ephemeral parameters.

deterministic_findings.recommendation: Configure the mail server to disable static RSA key exchange suites and prioritize ECDHE key exchange.

limitations: TLS selections come from ServerHello; observing ServerHello does not prove handshake completion or successful delivery.
TLS 1.3 certificates are encrypted. Chain validation requires visible certificates, observed SNI, capture time, and SMS_TRUST_STORE. Revocation is not checked.
Capture SHA-256 and report hashes support integrity comparison, not source authentication or digital signatures.
Analysis reflects strictly traffic captured and visible within the submitted packet capture window.
Passive network observation cannot evaluate email clients or cryptographic capabilities absent from the capture.
Incomplete TCP streams or truncated TLS handshakes in capture boundaries may limit full capability assessment.
AI-assisted anomaly prioritization is relative strictly to the observed client population in this capture.
AI anomaly engine abstains from statistical ranking when the comparison population is insufficient (minimum 5 observed clients).
Encrypted application-layer email payload (message text, headers, attachments) is not decrypted.
Hardening Impact Simulation results reflect passive capability evidence only and do not modify live servers.
privacy_statement: Capture files can contain sensitive payloads and are processed locally by TShark. Temporary uploaded files are removed after analysis. Command arguments are discarded at the extraction boundary; generated investigations retain transport and certificate metadata rather than message bodies or authentication secrets. Reports may contain IP addresses, hostnames, and certificate identities. No network revocation lookup or cloud AI is used.

recommendations.action: Configure the mail server to mandate STARTTLS before advertising or accepting AUTH commands.
recommendations.rationale: Authentication occurred before TLS protection was established.

recommendations.action: Enforce TLS encryption for all email communications using Direct TLS (e.g. port 465/993/995) or mandatory STARTTLS with strict rejection of unencrypted fallbacks.
recommendations.rationale: This email session continued without TLS protection, allowing application-layer traffic to traverse the observed network path without transport encryption.

recommendations.action: Configure the client and server policy to require TLS for this mail flow and reject insecure fallback where operationally appropriate.
recommendations.rationale: The server advertised STARTTLS, but the client continued the SMTP session without upgrading to TLS.

recommendations.action: Disable TLS 1.0 on 198.51.100.25 and configure the mail server to require TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 as the minimum acceptable protocol version.
recommendations.rationale: Observed email session negotiated deprecated TLS 1.0 protocol, which is susceptible to known downgrade attacks and lacks modern authenticated encryption.

recommendations.action: Disable obsolete cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, DES, EXPORT, NULL) on the mail server and require modern AEAD suites (e.g., AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305).
recommendations.rationale: The session negotiated weak or deprecated cipher suite TLS_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA, which is vulnerable to cryptanalytic attacks.

recommendations.action: Configure the mail server to disable static RSA key exchange suites and prioritize ECDHE key exchange.
recommendations.rationale: The session negotiated a static RSA key exchange cipher suite lacking Perfect Forward Secrecy. Compromise of the server private key allows retroactive decryption of past sessions.

recommendations.action: Maintain current TLS version baseline and monitor for future cryptographic standard updates.
recommendations.rationale: A currently accepted TLS protocol version (TLS 1.3) was observed.

recommendations.action: Renew invalid certificates, use modern keys, and supply an approved PEM trust store via SMS_TRUST_STORE for offline path validation. Check revocation separately.
recommendations.rationale: No server certificate is visible. TLS 1.3 encrypts certificates; a partial or resumed handshake may also omit them.
